# GOGJ — Japanese play impressions

- Original source: [『Robin Hood: The Legend of Sherwood』 プレイ感想](https://gogj.tokyo/2021/12/26/robin-hood-the-legend-of-sherwood-review/)
- Author / publication: あまがや; GOGJ.
- Language / date: Japanese; 2021-12-26.
- Access: Full article and both comments retrieved directly
- Checked: 2026-09-09
- Retrieved: 2026-09-09
- Archived copy: lookup failed (archive.org rate limit); not checked
- Format: header notes, original summary, then complete factual notes (unlicensed blog, not transcribed)

The author enjoys analyzing guard placement and coordinating character skills, while acknowledging dated controls and pacing. They highlight mouse-directed swordplay, camp training and production, party selection, optional civilian requests, and later territorial conflict as additions to the stealth formula.

The review interprets recruitment rewards for avoiding kills as encouragement toward stealth without removing aggressive alternatives. It mentions Japanese localization methods but supplies no instructions. In a January 2022 comment, the author says their playthrough remains unfinished, so this should be treated as play impressions rather than a completed-campaign assessment.

## Detailed notes

Page facts: title "『Robin Hood: The Legend of Sherwood』 プレイ感想" (play impressions); category レビュー (review); published 2021.12.26; author あまがや (Amagaya, author slug meatlizer); no numeric score; two comments (Good Old Gamer, 2022-01-11 12:52 PM; reply by あまがや, 2022-01-11 4:14 PM); retrieved directly from gogj.tokyo (site copyright 2026 GOGJ, no licence statement). Blog content, not transcribed.

Article content, in order:

- The author played this "somewhat old" title: an RTS on the Robin Hood theme, released 2002, developed by Spellbound Studios, makers of Desperados. Like Desperados it is a Commandos-like real-time strategy game controlling a small group, centred on stealth, coordination and reinforcement/replenishment.
- A Japanese localisation method exists; the article deliberately does not give details and tells readers to search for it. The GOG version "needs a little work" to apply it.
- Section 感想 (impressions): "really fun". Present-day controls and pacing are far away, so one must overlook that, but stealth strategy is enjoyable.
- Each character's distinctive skills and the synergy of combining them give many options in stealth play; matching options to situations and carrying a plan to success is the appeal, and "addictive".
- Analysing enemy placement and map structure, reading the intent behind a situation, then choosing a method: planning like a puzzle, not easy, but the author loves it.
- The game had "unexpected extra elements" that do not kill the core stealth, and fit Robin Hood:
  - Elaborate mouse-controlled sword fighting, which gives the option of deliberately engaging enemies.
  - A base element: gather companions, raise abilities through training, and produce items; character development must be considered to progress.
  - Choosing which companions to take on a sortie, allowing varied plans.
  - Optional side quests from townsperson NPCs, not required to clear missions; a good touch for Robin's chivalrous-thief character.
  - From around the middle of the story the power struggle intensifies and a real war element is added.
- Planning that assumes combat is possible, but stealth is still what is rewarded: repeated no-kill play makes companions gather more easily, which makes the mid-game-onward war events run relatively favourably. The game is designed to encourage stealth, yet the abundance of options to ignore that is stressed.
- The author cannot think of another medieval-themed stealth strategy game, and having development elements is rare; "very much worth playing".

Comments:

- Good Old Gamer (2022-01-11 12:52 PM): also likes the game; the slightly comical movements are fun just to watch; they had abandoned it midway and intend to resume after reading this.
- あまがや (2022-01-11 4:14 PM): glad to be the trigger; the author is also currently leaving it unfinished midway, and should have played it much earlier.
